accepted.s: Which Gupta ruler is regarded as the real founder of the Gupta Empire and ruled approximately from 319 to 335 CE?
accepted.x: Chandragupta I, who ruled approximately from 319 to 335 CE, is regarded as the real founder of the Gupta Empire.
accepted.tq: Use direct ruler-identification from the title or role associated with the ruler.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta I - marriage alliance, era started, first Gupta coins, queens of Gupta kings

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the territorial base of Chandragupta I:
1. His authority extended over South Bihar.
2. Saketa and Prayaga formed part of his dominions.
3. Pataliputra was his capital.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Chandragupta I ruled South Bihar and parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh, including Saketa and Prayaga, with Pataliputra as his capital.
accepted.tq: Combine territorial, capital and administrative facts, checking whether all statements belong to the same ruler.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta I - marriage alliance, era started, first Gupta coins, queens of Gupta kings

accepted.s: The marriage of Chandragupta I with Kumaradevi was significant primarily because it:
o: secured control over the western seaboard
gave the Guptas legitimacy and political strength through the Lichchhavis
ended the Gupta conflict with the Sakas
established matrimonial relations with the Vakatakas
accepted.x: Kumaradevi was a Lichchhavi princess, and the marriage enhanced Gupta legitimacy, prestige and political power.
accepted.tq: Identify the political consequence of a dynastic marriage rather than merely recalling the name.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta I - marriage alliance, era started, first Gupta coins, queens of Gupta kings

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Kumaradevi was the queen of Chandragupta I. Duttadevi, Kuberanaga and Anantadevi were associated with Samudragupta, Chandragupta II and Kumaragupta I respectively.
accepted.tq: Use king–queen association and eliminate the swapped matrimonial pairs.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta I - marriage alliance, era started, first Gupta coins, queens of Gupta kings

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (King)
A. Chandragupta I
B. Samudragupta
C. Chandragupta II
D. Kumaragupta I

List-II (Queen)
1. Anantadevi
2. Kumaradevi
3. Duttadevi
4. Kuberanaga

Which of the following is correct?
accepted.x: Chandragupta I–Kumaradevi, Samudragupta–Duttadevi, Chandragupta II–Kuberanaga and Kumaragupta I–Anantadevi are the correct pairs.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure king–queen pair and eliminate codes containing a swapped pair.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta I - marriage alliance, era started, first Gupta coins, queens of Gupta kings

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Gupta matrimonial links is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Dhruvadevi was associated first with Ramagupta and subsequently with Chandragupta II; therefore the pair presenting Ramagupta alone with the relationship is incomplete and is not correctly matched. Chandragupta II married Kuberanaga, while Prabhavati Gupta was married to Rudrasena II.
accepted.tq: Find the option that distorts a linked sequence rather than simply swapping two names.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta I - marriage alliance, era started, first Gupta coins, queens of Gupta kings

accepted.s: The early Gupta gold coins showing Chandragupta I and Kumaradevi are generally known as the:
accepted.x: The first Gupta gold coins issued by Chandragupta I are the King-Queen type, depicting Chandragupta I and Kumaradevi in association with the Lichchhavis.
accepted.tq: Distinguish coin types by the figures represented on them.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta I - marriage alliance, era started, first Gupta coins, queens of Gupta kings

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence in the early Gupta line?
accepted.x: The early Gupta succession is Sri Gupta, followed by Ghatotkacha, and then Chandragupta I.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last rulers before checking the middle succession.
accepted.sec: Gupta origin debate - caste, original home

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the origin of the Guptas:
1. Their origin is regarded as certain and undisputed.
2. They rose from relatively modest beginnings.
3. Their caste identity has been debated.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The origin of the Guptas is uncertain and debated. They rose from modest beginnings, and their caste identity has also been disputed.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute statement when the historical issue is expressly described as debated.
accepted.sec: Gupta origin debate - caste, original home

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements best reflects the debate regarding the caste origin of the Guptas?
o: They were exclusively Shudras according to all inscriptions.
Their caste origin is established by the Junagadh inscription.
They were universally accepted as Kshatriyas from the beginning.
They were originally Vaishyas, later treated by Brahmanas as Kshatriyas; a Brahmana origin has also been argued.
accepted.x: The Guptas are described as originally Vaishyas who were later treated as Kshatriyas by Brahmanas; a Brahmana origin has also been proposed on the basis of the Dharana gotra.
accepted.tq: Separate the commonly stated view from an alternative scholarly argument instead of treating one claim as conclusive.
accepted.sec: Gupta origin debate - caste, original home

accepted.s: Sri Gupta is associated with which of the following regions as his early sphere of authority?
accepted.x: Sri Gupta is stated to have ruled a small part of North Bengal and South Bihar.
accepted.tq: Use precise geographical discrimination among nearby historical regions.
accepted.sec: Gupta origin debate - caste, original home

accepted.s: The earliest Gupta political territory is described as comprising primarily:
o: Magadha, Prayaga and eastern Uttar Pradesh
accepted.x: The early Gupta territory was centred on Magadha, Prayaga and eastern Uttar Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Match the dynasty’s formative territorial core rather than its later expansion.
accepted.sec: Gupta origin debate - caste, original home

accepted.s: Which inscription provides evidence regarding Chandragupta II's conquests in the north-west and Bengal?
accepted.x: The Mehrauli iron pillar inscription is associated with Chandragupta II and refers to his conquests in the north-west and Bengal.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–inscription association to distinguish similar Gupta epigraphic sources.
accepted.sec: Sources - inscriptions (Allahabad, Eran, Mehrauli, Bhitari, Junagadh of Skandagupta), coins, Puranas, Devichandraguptam

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Eran inscription — Governors called Lokapala
2. Bhitari pillar — Defeat of the Hunas
3. Junagadh inscription — Repair of the Sudarshana lake
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Eran source refers to governors called Lokapala, the Bhitari pillar records Skandagupta's defeat of the Hunas, and the Junagadh inscription records the repair of the Sudarshana lake.
accepted.tq: Verify each source–content pair independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Sources - inscriptions (Allahabad, Eran, Mehrauli, Bhitari, Junagadh of Skandagupta), coins, Puranas, Devichandraguptam

accepted.s: Who was the governor responsible for repairing the Sudarshana lake during the reign of Skandagupta?
accepted.x: Parnadatta, the governor of Skandagupta, was responsible for the repair of the Sudarshana lake, as recorded in the Junagadh inscription.
accepted.tq: Identify the official connected with a public work rather than the ruler named in the inscription.
accepted.sec: Sources - inscriptions (Allahabad, Eran, Mehrauli, Bhitari, Junagadh of Skandagupta), coins, Puranas, Devichandraguptam

accepted.s: The Eran inscription of the Gupta period is associated with which of the following statements?
o: It refers to governors designated as Lokapala.
It records the Sri Lankan request for a monastery at Bodh Gaya.
It describes Chandragupta II's western conquests.
accepted.x: The Eran inscription is associated with Samudragupta and refers to governors called Lokapala.
accepted.tq: Eliminate options belonging to other inscriptions, literary works or diplomatic records.
accepted.sec: Sources - inscriptions (Allahabad, Eran, Mehrauli, Bhitari, Junagadh of Skandagupta), coins, Puranas, Devichandraguptam

accepted.s: The work Devichandraguptam, attributed to Vishakhadatta, deals with the episode involving:
accepted.x: Devichandraguptam narrates the episode involving Ramagupta, Dhruvadevi and Chandragupta II.
accepted.tq: Match a literary work with its distinctive dramatis personae.
accepted.sec: Sources - inscriptions (Allahabad, Eran, Mehrauli, Bhitari, Junagadh of Skandagupta), coins, Puranas, Devichandraguptam

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Mudrarakshasa — Political drama concerning Chanakya and Chandragupta Maurya
accepted.x: Mudrarakshasa, written by Vishakhadatta, is a political drama concerning Chanakya and Chandragupta Maurya. Devichandraguptam is also associated with Vishakhadatta, while the Prayaga Prasasti was composed by Harishena.
accepted.tq: Use author–work–subject combinations and reject cross-linked distractors.
accepted.sec: Sources - inscriptions (Allahabad, Eran, Mehrauli, Bhitari, Junagadh of Skandagupta), coins, Puranas, Devichandraguptam

accepted.s: Which of the following literary sources is particularly useful for information about the early territorial extent of the Gupta Empire?
accepted.x: The Puranas, including the Vayu Purana, describe the early Gupta territory.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a geographical source from literary works dealing with political drama or statecraft.
accepted.sec: Sources - inscriptions (Allahabad, Eran, Mehrauli, Bhitari, Junagadh of Skandagupta), coins, Puranas, Devichandraguptam

accepted.s:
Gupta coins are important historical sources because they provide evidence about:
1. Royal titles
2. Religious affiliations
3. Ritual practices and prosperity
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Gupta coins, mostly gold, depict rulers, deities and rituals and thereby reveal royal titles, religious ideas, ritual practices and the prosperity of the period.
accepted.tq: Recognise the multiple kinds of historical information conveyed by coin evidence.
accepted.sec: Sources - inscriptions (Allahabad, Eran, Mehrauli, Bhitari, Junagadh of Skandagupta), coins, Puranas, Devichandraguptam

accepted.s: Which ruler sent an embassy to Samudragupta seeking permission to build a monastery and a rest house at Bodh Gaya?
accepted.x: Meghavarman, the Buddhist ruler of Sri Lanka, sent a mission to Samudragupta for permission to build a monastery and rest house at Bodh Gaya.
accepted.tq: Identify the foreign ruler and the diplomatic purpose together.
accepted.sec: Foreign contacts - Sri Lankan embassy to the Gupta court

accepted.s: The embassy of Meghavarman to the Gupta court is known primarily through:
accepted.x: The mission of Meghavarman and the request concerning Bodh Gaya are recorded in a Chinese source.
accepted.tq: Separate the event from the different types of sources used to record it.
accepted.sec: Foreign contacts - Sri Lankan embassy to the Gupta court

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Gupta foreign relations:
1. Kushanas and Sakas paid homage to the Gupta ruler.
2. Kings of Southeast Asia and Ceylon sent tribute.
3. Gupta foreign contacts were confined entirely to northern India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Kushanas and Sakas paid homage, while rulers of Southeast Asia and Ceylon sent tribute. Gupta foreign contacts were not confined entirely to northern India.
accepted.tq: Spot the geographically extreme statement that conflicts with the wider diplomatic evidence.
accepted.sec: Foreign contacts - Sri Lankan embassy to the Gupta court

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Chandragupta II's external commercial links is correct?
o: His trade was restricted to the Himalayan region.
His trade routes bypassed the western sea entirely.
His sea trade reached Europe through Egypt.
His maritime contacts were limited to Sri Lanka alone.
accepted.x: Chandragupta II's sea trade reached Europe via Egypt, indicating wide-ranging maritime commercial contacts.
accepted.tq: Use the route detail to distinguish a precise trade statement from restrictive distractors.
accepted.sec: Foreign contacts - Sri Lankan embassy to the Gupta court

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Fa-Hien is correct?
o: He visited India during Samudragupta's reign and described the Allahabad inscription.
He was an ambassador sent by Meghavarman of Sri Lanka.
He explicitly names Chandragupta II as the ruler under whom he travelled.
He travelled in the empire of Chandragupta II but did not name the king.
accepted.x: Fa-Hien travelled in the empire of Chandragupta II, but his account does not name the king directly.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the period identified through historical reconstruction from the name explicitly mentioned by the traveller.
accepted.sec: Foreign contacts - Sri Lankan embassy to the Gupta court

accepted.s: Which type of Samudragupta's coinage portrays him as a poet and musician?
accepted.x: The lyrist or veena-player type depicts Samudragupta as a poet-musician and supports the association of the title Kaviraja with him.
accepted.tq: Match a coin type with the distinctive activity depicted on it.
accepted.sec: Samudragupta's coins - types (lyrist, ashvamedha, archer)

accepted.s: The Ashvamedha type of Samudragupta's coins was issued after he:
o: received the embassy from Sri Lanka
accepted.x: Samudragupta issued the Ashvamedha type after performing the Ashvamedha, or horse sacrifice.
accepted.tq: Connect a commemorative coin type with the event it celebrates.
accepted.sec: Samudragupta's coins - types (lyrist, ashvamedha, archer)

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a type of coin attributed to Samudragupta?
accepted.x: The King-Queen type belongs to the coinage of Chandragupta I, whereas Samudragupta issued lyrist, Ashvamedha and archer types among others.
accepted.tq: Identify the coin type belonging to a different ruler.
accepted.sec: Samudragupta's coins - types (lyrist, ashvamedha, archer)

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains only coin types associated with Samudragupta?
accepted.x: Lyrist, Ashvamedha and archer are all types of Samudragupta's coinage. The King-Queen type belongs to Chandragupta I, while the other options combine unrelated descriptions.
accepted.tq: Test the whole set and reject options containing a coin type of another ruler.
accepted.sec: Samudragupta's coins - types (lyrist, ashvamedha, archer)
